These ratios can differ arbitrarily, so the assumption lambda_max < 1 is not automatically removable by scaling.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: Numerical methods can be applied to solve equation \eqref{alpha*}.

issues.failure_explanation: If C < 1, then log(C alpha) < 0 for alpha < 1/C, so the objective tends to -infinity as alpha approaches 1 from above. Hence there is no minimum over alpha > 1, and the derivative equation may have no solution. C can be < 1 under the stated assumptions (e.g., when lambda_min is close to lambda_max, lambda_max is close to 1, and n is large).
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Restrict the optimization to C > 1, or replace log(C alpha) by max(1, log(C alpha)) and solve the resulting constrained optimization.
issues.overall_effect: The claimed optimized error allocation is not well-posed for all parameter regimes; the numerical solution of the alpha* equation may fail to exist.
issues.title: Optimization problem may have no minimizer when C < 1
issues.why_classification: The optimization technique is a central contribution, but a contained fix (constraint or case split) preserves the general approach.
